output.title: When template reuse is worth measuring
output.body:
If you run a small business, template reuse is only worth measuring when it becomes a workflow decision, not a tidy dashboard exercise.

The useful question is simple: which one recurring template matters enough that you would act on the data? That could be customer emails, proposals, intake forms, or invoice layouts. If you cannot name the workflow, measuring reuse usually turns into noise.

The next step is manual: audit one month of one workflow by hand. List the templates you actually used, where they live, and whether you can tell which version is current. That gives you a real read on whether reuse is visible enough to count.

This is also the boundary for automation. A reuse-counting system only makes sense if the templates live in a central, searchable place and the definition of “reuse” is clear. If the files are scattered across inboxes, shared folders, and desktops, the first fix is usually organisation, not automation.

And if the audit shows the same template keeps showing up in different places, that is the signal to measure it more formally. The owner still decides whether to consolidate or retire anything; software should surface the pattern, not make the call.
